parole.significato: angel (an incorporeal and holy or semidivine messenger from a deity or other divine entity)
parole.testo: From Late Latin angelus (“angel”), from Ancient Greek ἄγγελος (ángelos, “messenger”).

parole.significato: apoplexy, stroke (a sudden interruption of blood supply to the brain)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin poplexia, apoplexia, from Ancient Greek ἀποπληξίᾱ (apoplēxíā), from ἀποπλήσσω (apoplḗssō, “to cripple by a stroke”); ἀπο- (apo-, “from”) + πλήσσω (plḗssō, “to strike”).
Borrowed from Late Latin apostolus, from Ancient Greek ἀπόστολος (apóstolos, “one who is sent”; “messenger”, “envoy”, “ambassador”; “Apostle”).

parole.significato: aristocracy (the nobility, or the hereditary ruling class)
parole.testo: From Late Latin aristocratia, from Ancient Greek ἀριστοκρατία (aristokratía, “aristocracy”), from ἄριστος (áristos, “best”) + κράτος (krátos, “power”).

parole.significato: archangel (a powerful angel that leads many other angels)
parole.testo: From Late Latin archangelus, from Ancient Greek ἀρχάγγελος (arkhángelos, “archangel”), from the prefix ἀρχι- (arkhi-), from ἄρχω (árkhō, “to begin, lead, rule”) + ἄγγελος (ángelos, “messenger”).
Borrowed from Late Latin diphthongus, from Ancient Greek δίφθογγος (díphthongos, “diphthong”), from δι- (di-, “two”) + φθόγγος (phthóngos, “sound”).

parole.significato: dose (a measured portion of medicine taken at any one time)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis, “a portion prescribed”, literally “a giving”), from δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to give”). First attested in 1735. With -ózis ending.
From Late Latin eleēmosyna (“alms”), from Ancient Greek ἐλεημοσύνη (eleēmosúnē, “pity, mercy”). Doublet of alamizsna.

parole.significato: embolism (an obstruction or occlusion of a blood vessel by a blood clot, air bubble or other matter)
parole.testo: Internationalism from Late Latin embolismus, Ancient Greek ἐμβολισμός (embolismós, “intercalary”), from ἐμβάλλω (embállō, “to insert, throw in”).
From Late Latin epidēmia, from Ancient Greek ἐπιδήμιος (epidḗmios).
From Late Latin Pharaō, from Ancient Greek Φαραώ (Pharaṓ), from Hebrew פַּרְעֹה (par‘ōh), from Egyptian pr-ꜥꜣ (“great house; pharaoh”).

From Late Latin gingiber, from Latin zingiberī, from Ancient Greek ζιγγίβερις (zingíberis), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀺𑀁𑀕𑀺𑀯𑁂𑀭 (siṃgivera), 𑀲𑀺𑀁𑀕𑀯𑁂𑀭 (siṃgavera), from Sanskrit शृङ्गवेर (śṛṅgavera), from Dravidian roots, compare Tamil இஞ்சி (iñci, “ginger”) + வேர் (vēr, “root”).
From Late Latin monogamia, from Ancient Greek μονογαμία (monogamía).

parole.significato: magic (the use of rituals or actions, especially based on supernatural or occult knowledge)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin magia, from Ancient Greek μαγεία (mageía).
From Late Latin oligarcha, from Ancient Greek ὀλιγάρχης (oligárkhēs, “oligarch”).

parole.significato: paradigm (a pattern, a way of doing something; especially a pattern of thought, a system of beliefs, a conceptual frame…
parole.testo: From Late Latin paradīgma, from Ancient Greek παράδειγμα (parádeigma, “pattern”).
From Late Latin polygamia, from Ancient Greek πολυγαμία (polugamía), itself from πολύγαμος (polúgamos, “married to many”), from πολύς (polús, “many”) + γάμος (gámos, “marriage”).

parole.significato: syncope (missed beat or off-beat stress in music resulting in syncopation)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Late Latin syncopē, from Ancient Greek σῠγκοπή (sŭnkopḗ, “cutting up; syncope”), from συγκόπτω (sunkóptō, “to cut up”) + -η (-ē, nominalization suffix).

parole.significato: amen (at the end of religious prayers: so be it)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin amen, from Ancient Greek ἀμήν (amḗn, “so be it”), from Hebrew אמן (āmēn, “truly, certainly”).
